summary:
Mission Orbit is a browser game where players design, manage and fly a complete space mission. In the Mission Architect, you pick a science goal (track a hurricane, map wildfires, or search for life on Mars), choose instruments, an orbit, a spacecraft bus and a launch vehicle, then balance mass, power, data, cost and schedule on a budget sheet and defend the design at review gates. 

You then fly the mission yourself with real orbital mechanics: launch through storms, reach orbit, photograph live targets, downlink data, dock with a station, land the booster, or cruise to Mars and operate a rover. A debrief pairs every design decision with what it caused in flight.

It addresses the challenge by making engineering trade-offs playable, so players see how each choice shapes mission success. It matters because it teaches systems thinking with live NASA data, in plain language, free in any browser with no install or sign-up.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Mission Orbit takes a player through the whole life of a space mission.

1. Design. The Mission Architect has seven steps: science goal, requirements (a science traceability matrix), orbit, spacecraft bus, launch vehicle, budget sheet and review gates. The budget sheet tracks mass, power, data, cost and schedule margins. Review gates draw risk events, and if reserves run out the player must descope or be cancelled.

2. Fly. The player launches and flies the mission by hand in a 3D scene driven by an orbital-mechanics model: weather holds, staging, storms, debris, radiation storms, photography passes, data downlink, station rendezvous, de-orbit and booster landing.

3. Operate. Mars missions continue through a trans-Mars injection burn, a cruise with a trajectory-correction decision, and rover operations in Jezero Crater, planned one Martian day at a time.

4. Learn. The debrief shows each decision next to what it caused, a 40-flight Monte Carlo study shows how reliable a design is, and a mentor, Dr. Ada Reyes, explains each phase aloud.

There are also four short training missions, a Daily Launch that is the same for every player, a guided tour, and shareable design links.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Players learn systems thinking: a choice in one subsystem becomes a cost in another. Every technical term is given in plain words first, with a glossary, so no background is needed. It runs free in a browser with no install or account, falls back to archived NASA data when the live feeds are unreachable, and supports keyboard play and reduced motion, so it suits classrooms and self-learners.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

The design rules are modelled on real NASA practice (margins, concept maturity levels, review gates, lightning launch rules) and cite their sources inside the game. Live NASA feeds change the game each day: real storms and wildfires become photo targets, and real solar flares become radiation storms. The music is generated live in code and follows the mission.

TOOLS AND LANGUAGES

JavaScript, React 19, three.js, Vite, Web Audio API, WebGL. Blender with Python for the rover model. Python (numpy, Pillow) for generated Mars textures. Kokoro-82M text-to-speech for the mentor's voice. Hosted on Vercel. No backend: progress is saved in the browser.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Accuracy against playability (the planet is scaled down so an orbit takes minutes), performance on integrated graphics, accessibility (not relying on colour alone), and keeping screens uncluttered by showing the state first and the explanation on request.
